text:
Dumping LSASS memory is a credential-harvesting technique — the output contains password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and sometimes plaintext credentials. Writing a tool for that isn't something I can help with, regardless of network ownership framing.

If you have a legitimate defensive need — like testing whether your EDR detects LSASS access — the standard approach is to use a known, audited tool (Sysinternals ProcDump, Windows Task Manager, or WinPmem) in a controlled lab environment, rather than a custom one-off binary that would likely trip fewer detection rules.

Happy to help with other Windows systems work.
